title: Cardiac Spheroids as in vitro Bioengineered Heart Tissues to Study Human Heart Pathophysiology
protocol: Thaw cryovials containing HCFs and HCAECs in a water bath at 37°C for one minute.

Collect 1 mL of cell suspension from the cryovials using a 1000 μL pipette tip and add into a 15 mL tube containing 7 mL of Human Cardiac Fibroblast Medium for HCFs and 7 mL of Human Meso Endo Growth Medium for HCAECs.
Rinse cells twice with 1 mL of culture medium from the same 15 mL tube to collect the majority of the cells.
Gently mix cell suspensions.
Transfer cell suspensions to separate T75 culture flasks using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Incubate cells at 37°C with 5% CO2.
After 18 h, aspirate the medium from both culture flasks and rinse them once with sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Replace PBS with 7 mL of appropriate culture medium to each culture flask and incubate at 37°C.
Examine cellular expansion and viability regularly and replace media every other day until cells reach 80-90% confluency.
Pre-coat two T25 culture flasks with 2 mL of PBS containing 40 µg/mL of fibronectin (FN) and incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for at least 4 hours.
After 4 hours, collect one cryovial containing iCMs and place it in a water bath at 37 °C for 4 min.
Move the cryovial under a sterile laminar flow biosafety cabinet class 2.
Transfer the iCMs from the cryovial to a sterile 50 mL centrifuge tube using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Rinse the empty iCMs cryovial with 1 mL of room temperature plating medium.
Transfer the 1 mL of plating medium rinse from the cryovial drop-wise over 90 sec to the 50 mL centrifuge tube containing the iCM cell suspension.
Gently swirl the tube while adding the medium to mix the solution completely and decrease the osmotic shock on the thawed cells.
Slowly add 8 mL of room temperature Plating Medium to the 50 mL centrifuge tube, starting with the first 1 mL dropwise over 30 - 60 s.
Add the remaining volume over the next 30 s while gently swirling the tube.
Gently mix the contents of the 50 mL centrifuge tube by inverting 2 - 3 times (avoiding vigorous shaking or vortexing).
Immediately perform cell counting using a hemocytometer to determine viable cell density.
Take FN-pre-coated T25 flasks and aspirate the FN-PBS solution without letting the flasks dry.
Add seeding volume of iCMs (1.6 x 10^6 viable iCMs in 8 mL room temperature plating medium) to each flask.
Culture iCMs in the incubator for 48 h at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Thaw Maintenance Medium overnight at 4 °C a day before use.
Equilibrate the Maintenance Medium in a 37 °C water bath and use immediately.
Gently wash off dead cells and debris by gently pipetting the Plating Medium up and down 5 times.
Aspirate the Plating Medium and replace with 8 mL of pre-warmed Maintenance Medium.
Replace the Maintenance Medium every other day and examine the confluency regularly.
Collect HCAECs and HCFs following steps 3.2-3.12.
Prepare CS culture medium by mixing 10 mL of iCMs Maintenance Medium, 5 mL of Human Cardiac Fibroblast Medium, and 5 mL of Meso Endo Growth Medium.
Remove the culture medium from each tissue flask containing HCFs and rinse once with 5 mL PBS for T75 flasks.
Add 5 mL of 0.25% trypsin EDTA solution to each T75 flask and incubate for 5 min at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Neutralize the trypsin EDTA solution with 5 mL of culture medium once cells detach.
Transfer cell suspensions to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge cells at 300 x g for 4 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully from each tube.
Add 1 mL of CS medium to each cell pellet and resuspend them.
Keep the tube on ice and count cells using Trypan Blue and a hemocytometer.
Remove Maintenance Medium from tissue flasks containing iCMs.
Rinse once with 3 mL of PBS.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% trypsin EDTA solution to each T75 flask and incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Check cells every minute until detached.
Neutralize the trypsin EDTA solution with 4 mL of culture medium once cells detach.
Transfer cell suspensions to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge them at 300 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully from each tube.
Add 1 mL of culture medium to the cell pellet and resuspend it.
Keep the tube on ice and count cells using Trypan Blue and a hemocytometer.
Mix iCMs, HCFs and HCAECs in a 2:1:1 ratio by plating 10,000 iCMs, 5,000 HCFs and 5,000 HCAECs per hanging drop culture containing 20 µL of CS medium.
Adjust to the final volume for the total number of CSs.
Pipette 20 μl of cell suspension into each well of the 384 well HDC plate either manually or by using a robotic multichannel pipette for automated liquid handling.
Pipette 1.5 mL of sterile PBS in each side of the channel around the Hanging Drop Plate to prevent drying out CSs.
Incubate HDC plate at 37 °C.
Examine formation of CSs on a daily basis until a fully formed spheroid is observed in the majority of wells.
Add 7.5 μL of CS medium to each well every other day until a CS is formed.
Collect CSs with a 1 mL pipette tip.
Cut the tip of the pipette around 0.2 cm from the edge using a sterile sharp surface.
Collect the CS suspension into a 50 mL tube on ice.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 x g for 5 min.
Keep the pellet on ice until use.
Prepare a collagen gel solution (100 µL/well for 7.5 mL total) on ice using rat tail collagen and CS medium in a 3:7 ratio.
Remove the supernatant from the tube containing CSs.
Mix the pelleted CSs within the collagen gel solution.
Add 1 µL/mL of 5 mM sodium hydroxide to the CS-collagen gel suspension and mix gently.
Transfer 100 µL of CS-collagen gel to a clear flat bottom 96 well black polystyrene microplate.
Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Prepare a 10 µM DOX solution based on previously established protocol for cell death in CSs.
Add 100 µL of solutions containing DOX and/or other agents to each well.
Incubate the plate for 18 h at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Collect the Live/Dead staining reagent stock solutions and allow them to thaw on ice in the dark in a biosafety cabinet.
Prepare a solution containing Hoechst stain, 4 µM ethidium homodimer, and 2 µM calcein-AM.
Add 100 μL of the Hoechst stain, calcein-AM/ethidium homodimer solution into each well.
Measure fluorescence in each well at 645 nm for ethidium homodimer and at 530 nm for calcein-AM using a multimode microplate reader.
Transfer fluorescence measurements to Graphpad PRISM or equivalent software for statistical analysis.
Check under an epifluorescence microscope for nuclei staining, together with calcein-AM and ethidium homodimer.
Collect CSs from collagen gels using a 1 mL pipette tip cut 0.5 mm from the edge.
Transfer collected CSs to a falcon tube containing media to prevent drying.
Place each CS (with some µL of media) on the stage of the IonOptix system one at a time.
Select the CS to be analyzed by setting peaks on both sides using the IonOptix software.
Stabilize both the peaks adjusting threshold and edge options from the computer.
Expose CSs to different frequencies (0.3, 0.6, 1, 2 and 3 Hz) and voltages (1, 2, 3 and 5 V) using the Myopacer Field Stimulator.
Record spheroid shortening as CS length changes of DOX-treated and untreated CSs.
Analyse data using the Soft-Edge software and averaged for each CS.
Collect the 96 well plate after 30 min.
Fix CSs in 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 1 h at room temperature.
Remove PFA and rinse three times with PBS containing 0.01% sodium azide (PBSA).
Add 200 µL of PBSA containing 0.02% Triton-X-100 to each well for 30 min on a shaker.
Add 200 µL of 3% bovine serum albumin in PBSA solution for 60 min at room temperature.
Prepare a solution containing 10 µg/mL of primary mouse anti-human antibodies against CD31 diluted in blocking solution.
Add 100 µL of primary antibody solution to each well and incubate overnight at 4 °C on a shaker.
Rinse the plate three times with PBSA for 20 min at room temperature on a rocking plate.
Prepare a solution containing Hoechst DNA stain and 10 µg/mL of Cy3-conjugated secondary donkey anti-mouse antibody diluted in blocking solution.
Add 100 μL of the secondary antibody solution containing Hoechst stain to each well.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C on a shaker.
Cover the plate with aluminium foil.
Rinse the plate three times for 20 min with PBSA at room temperature on a rocking plate.
Add 100 μL of Vectashield mounting medium to each well.
Image CSs under a laser scanning confocal microscope.
Perform optical sectioning along the Z axis.
Collapse images into a single focal plane using ImageJ software.
